short: The decisive engagement of the First English Civil War, where the New Model Army destroyed King Charles I's main veteran field army.
full:
On 14 June 1645, the Parliamentarian New Model Army engaged King Charles I's main field army near the village of Naseby in Northamptonshire. Despite being heavily outnumbered, the Royalist forces launched an aggressive early attack that initially pushed back the Parliamentarian infantry. However, Prince Rupert's Royalist cavalry again left the field to pursue the enemy baggage train, fatally exposing the king's center.

Oliver Cromwell, commanding the Parliamentarian cavalry on the right wing, routed his opposition but kept his troopers disciplined and on the battlefield. He then directed them into the flanks and rear of the Royalist infantry, causing a total collapse. Charles lost his veteran infantry, all his artillery, and his personal baggage—which contained letters revealing his attempts to bring foreign Catholic troops into England, destroying his political credibility and ending any realistic hope of a Royalist military victory.
